questions.q: Why doesn't this lesson have you run a `BACKUP DATABASE db-overlook-core TO DISK = ...` statement?
options: Because Overlook's database doesn't have Azure CLI access configured yet
Because full backups are only needed once per year
Azure SQL Database is PaaS — Microsoft takes full backups automatically, and there's no disk or BACKUP statement available to the DBA
Because BACKUP DATABASE is deprecated T-SQL syntax in all SQL Server versions
questions.explain: On the PaaS tier, Microsoft owns the backup mechanism entirely — BACKUP DATABASE only applies to SQL Server you manage directly, on-prem or on an Azure VM.

questions.q: When did Azure actually begin building the automated backup chain for db-overlook-core?
options: Backups don't start until the database has been live for 30 days
Only after the first differential backup is explicitly requested
The moment it finished provisioning in Lesson 3, with no action required from the DBA
Only after the DBA manually enables a backup toggle in the Portal
questions.explain: Azure begins its automated full/differential/log backup schedule as soon as the database exists — this lesson's job is to confirm it, not create it.

options: The scheduled time of the next full backup
The exact storage account path where backup files are saved
That a full backup already exists and the automated backup chain has started, by showing the oldest currently restorable point in time
The total number of backups taken so far
questions.explain: A non-null earliestRestoreDate is direct, verifiable proof that the automated backup chain exists — the same value shown in the Portal's restore dialog.

questions.q: Which of these does the DBA still control on Azure SQL Database, even without triggering backups directly?
options: The exact minute each full backup runs
Storage redundancy (LRS/ZRS/GRS) and the retention window the automated backups use
Whether COMPRESSION is applied to the backup file
Which disk path the backup file is written to
questions.explain: The DBA still controls redundancy tier and retention settings even though Microsoft owns the actual backup trigger and schedule on this platform.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say this is 'not a gap in the capstone' rather than a missing step?
options: Because the capstone will cover manual BACKUP DATABASE syntax in a later lesson instead
Because full backups aren't actually necessary for patient-record databases
Because it's the real, accurate behavior of Azure SQL Database as a PaaS platform, not an oversight in the project
Because Overlook's database is too small to need full backups
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this reflects the honest, documented behavior of Azure SQL Database (PaaS) — a genuine platform trade-off, not something left out of the course.
